# Candidate next unit: constructive CM-24 and a Frobenius eigenbasis

2026-10-15 UTC. Root EM-DVR-FBF223 author-side paper candidate for
unchanged owner EM-DIRECT-18F24A and support EM-CM24CONN-63E74C9D.
It is separate from the fixed MW precision note and is not yet reviewed.
No scientific code, selected prime, sample or new owner/claim.

Work at t²=1/2. The actual short curve is

    E_t:y²=x³+(12t-15)x+24-28t.

The point T=(-4t,0) is a rational point of order2. Indeed the
generic cubic value at -4t is -2(2t²-1)(16t+11). Put

    X=x+4t, a=-12t, b=9+12t,
    y²=X³+aX²+bX,
    b*b_(-t)=9,
    v=2t, v²=2, nu²=-3, w=nu*v, w²=-6.

Thus b is a unit at every original p>=13. The standard normalized
two-torsion quotient candidate is

    X_q=X+a+b/X,
    Y_q=y*(1-b/X²),
    E_q:Y_q²=X_q³-2aX_q²+(a²-4b)X_q.

Since -2a=24t=2a_(-t) and a²-4b=36-48t=4b_(-t), scaling
X_q=v² X_minus,Y_q=v³y_minus and translating back gives a map
k_t:E_t -> E_(-t) with SHORT coordinates

    x_minus=(x+b/(x+4t))/2,
    y_minus=y*(1-b/(x+4t)²)/(4t).

The exact curve identity, extension at T/O, degree2 and kernel
{O,T} should all be proved, rather than inferred solely from j.
For the specified bases omega=dx/(2y),eta=x dx/(2y), direct
relative differentiation gives

    d(y/X)=(X-b/X)omega,
    k_t^*omega_minus=v omega,
    k_t^*eta_minus=v eta+2tv omega-(v/2)d(y/X).

Hence its class-column matrix is K_t=v[[1,2t],[0,1]], determinant2.
All rational exact functions must remain visible for relative targets.

Compose the already proved j_(-t):E_(-t) -> E_t with k_t:

    alpha_t=j_(-t) o k_t,
    deg alpha_t=6,
    alpha_t^*omega=w omega,
    A_t=K_t J=w[[1,2(1-t)],[0,-1]].

In characteristic zero, alpha_t²=[-6] follows from the invariant
differential and injectivity of that representation on elliptic
endomorphisms. Prove it there first, then specialize the actual map
identity at good primes; zero differential after reduction alone
would not prove the identity. This embeds Z[sqrt(-6)], the maximal
order of discriminant-24, and would give a constructive CM model
identification independent of simply naming Sun's CM label.

The candidate exact diagonal cohomology basis is

    e_CM,t=(omega,psi_t), psi_t=eta+(t-1)omega,
    alpha_t^*e_CM,t=e_CM,t diag(w,-w).

At the halfpoint, psi_t=3*nabla_t omega-t*omega by the already
proved geometric connection. All basis changes are p-integral units.
The composed rational exact term is obtained by pulling back that
of j_(-t) together with the displayed k_t exact term; no endpoint
period is declared equal to a cohomology class.

For the original p, coefficient Frobenius sends t to -t, fixes nu
and sends w to -w. Genuine crystalline Frobenius commutes with
the endomorphism through coefficient conjugation. Thus, IF its
matrix is expressed from sigma(e_CM,t) to e_CM,t in the stated
column convention, the expected relation is

    diag(w,-w)*M_CM=M_CM*diag(-w,w),
    M_CM=[[0,B],[C,0]].

With the usual Frobenius cup-product determinantp, this would give
BC=-p. Determinant and Hodge divisibility conventions must be
checked, not presumed from an arbitrary transport. The unit B is
not determined here. In Weierstrass bases this form would be

    M_weier=[[ (t-1)C, B+(t²-1)C ],
              [ C,       (t+1)C ]], t²-1=-1/2.

This is a candidate exact CM constraint on the genuine matrix, not
a computation of B,C, the divided complementary endpoint or Y.
It supplies neither an ambient halfpoint first jet nor the full
weighted relative-functional bridge with H_b/quarter terms. Those,
all Y/Z/kappa values and all original parent goals remain OPEN.

Only this fixed source-bound map and its cohomology/Frobenius
constraint are proposed. Standard two-isogeny/CM facts are not
claimed globally novel; old three-isogeny and GM proofs are reused,
not rerun or edited. No new free correction or sample campaign.

# Constructive CM−24 and the genuine Frobenius matrix shape

2026-10-15. Separate fixed paper unit. Original owner
EM-DIRECT-18F24A and support EM-CM24CONN-63E74C9D unchanged.
Root EM-DVR-FBF223 supplied the two-isogeny/composite/CM-basis
candidate and is a mathematical coauthor, not a decisive reviewer.
Shared-context paper cross-checks are not formal independent review.
This proof is frozen for subsequent distinct review.

The fixed input is
`control/ROOT_CM24_EXPLICIT_DEGREE_SIX_CM_ENDOMORPHISM_CANDIDATE_20261015.md`,
3880B, SHA256c747cf16b2b58326ea1d5e28b3daceaa304d7d52c131c121679d88471d16c086.
The old geometry13972B, centre10360B and MW12956B originals are
not edited, rerun or included as new results. Their exact source
family, three-isogeny and geometric connection are reused. No new
sample, symbolic program, source search or unknown period fits a map.

## Ring and the fixed two-isogeny

Work first in characteristic zero with t²=1/2, nu²=−3, and then
over their good integral models at every original p≥13. Put

    E_t:y²=x³+(12t−15)x+24−28t,
    T=(−4t,0), z=x+4t,
    a=−12t, b=9+12t,
    v=2t, v²=2, w=nu*v, w²=−6.

All coefficients belong to
`Z[1/6,t,nu]/(2t²−1,nu²+3)`. The discriminant
6912(1−t)(1+t)³ is a unit there: `(1−t)(1+t)=1/2`.
Also `b*b_(−t)=9`, so b is a unit. The cubic becomes

    y²=z³+a z²+b z.                                 (1)

Thus T is a nonzero point of exact order2. Alternatively the
generic original cubic at x=−4t equals
`−2(2t²−1)(16t+11)`, verifying the source specialization explicitly.

The normalized quotient is

    X_q=z+a+b/z, Y_q=y(1−b/z²),
    E_q:Y_q²=X_q³−2a X_q²+(a²−4b)X_q.              (2)

Here is its entire curve-identity check. With L=z²+az+b,

    Y_q²=L(z²−b)²/z³,
    X_q[(X_q−a)²−4b]=L(z²−b)²/z³.                  (3)

Thus(2) follows exactly, without identifying curves solely by j.
Since dX_q/dz=1−b/z², the normalized invariant differential pulls
back to omega=dx/(2y). At T, z has zero order2 and y has zero
order1, so X_q has pole order2; it has the same pole order at O.
The rational map extends projectively at both points. Its degree is2,
its kernel is{O,T}, and its nonzero differential proves separability
at all these good characteristics. It is a group homomorphism
because it carries origin to origin.

For the translated model of E_(−t), a_(−t)=12t and b_(−t)=9−12t.
The identities

    −2a=2a_(−t), a²−4b=4b_(−t)

show that scaling X_q=v² z_-,Y_q=v³ y_- and translating back
gives the fixed degree-two isogeny k_t:E_t->E_(−t):

    x_-=(x+b/(x+4t))/2,
    y_-=y(1−b/(x+4t)²)/(4t).                       (4)

The scale is v=√2, not nu=√−3. All its coefficient denominators
are units at the original primes; the z-denominators describe the
kernel points, not a bad p-adic model.

## Literal exact terms and the whole degree-six kernel

Use omega_t=dx/(2y),eta_t=x dx/(2y). Differentiation of(1) gives

    d(y/z)=(z−b/z)omega_t,
    k_t^*omega_-=v omega_t,
    k_t^*eta_-=v eta_t+2tv omega_t−(v/2)d(y/z).       (5)

The last formula also follows immediately by inserting(4). In
cohomology, with columns equal to pullbacks of the TARGET basis
in the SOURCE basis, it is

    K_t=v[[1,2t],[0,1]], det K_t=2.                 (6)

Reuse the fixed j_(−t):E_(−t)->E_t of degree3 with
`J=nu[[1,2],[0,−1]]`. The composition

    alpha_t=j_(−t) o k_t:E_t->E_t

has degree6. Its kernel is exactly the following six distinct points:

    O, T, Q_t, −Q_t, P_t, −P_t,
    Q_t=(3,2(t+1)),
    P_t=T+Q_t=(3−4t,6(t−1)).                       (7)

For a direct check, preimages of x_-=3 satisfy
`(x−6)(x+4t)+b=(x−3)(x−3+4t)=0`. At those roots the two
pairs of y values are exactly those in(7). Their images are ±Q_-
and hence lie in the kernel of j_(−t). The points O,T map to O.
The six points are distinct because 2,3,t,t±1 and3±4t are units;
the last product is9−16t²=1. Together with deg alpha=6 this
proves the whole kernel. It is cyclic of order6, generated by P_t.

The literal rational exact term of the composition must remain
visible. Put

    G_t=(w/2)y/z−(2/nu) k_t^*(y_-/(x_-−3)).

Pulling back the previously proved j exact term gives

    alpha_t^*omega_t=w omega_t,
    alpha_t^*eta_t=2w(1−t)omega_t−w eta_t+dG_t.      (8)

If an explicit source rational function is desired, the second
term uses

    k_t^*(y_-/(x_-−3))
       =y(z²−b)/[v z((x−6)z+b)].                   (9)

All coefficient factors are integral units. Its possible poles lie
in the kernel(7) and have at most order1, since the constituent
isogenies are prime to p and the earlier primitive has simple poles.
The derivative has the corresponding double poles. The functions
in(5),(8),(9) are not being set to zero at any relative endpoint.
De Rham/Čech passage removes their exact CLASSES, not their
literal boundary values in the original research functional.

## Constructive CM and an integral eigenbasis

The class-column matrix from(8) is

    A_t=K_t J=w[[1,2(1−t)],[0,−1]], det A_t=6.       (10)

To prove the endomorphism identity, first work in characteristic
zero. Both alpha_t² and[−6] have invariant differential−6.
Their difference as elliptic endomorphisms has zero differential
and must be zero: a nonzero characteristic-zero elliptic
endomorphism is a separable isogeny. Thus

    alpha_t²=[−6].                                  (11)

This is proved before reduction and extends as an identity of the
good integral maps. It is not inferred from zero differential in
characteristic p. The polarized dual is−alpha_t by degree6 and(11).
The map `Z[√−6] -> End(E_t)` given by √−6↦alpha_t is injective
in characteristic zero, for its differential sends a+b√−6 to
a+bw. It embeds the MAXIMAL order: squarefree−6≡2mod4, so the
ring of integers is Z[√−6], with discriminant−24.

For completeness, the characteristic-zero geometric endomorphism
ring is exactly that order, rather than an unspecified larger one.
After complex embedding, endomorphisms act as complex scalars on a
rank-two period lattice. They commute with w and hence lie in the
two-dimensional rational centralizer Q(w); their integral action
on the lattice makes them algebraic integers. They are therefore
contained in its maximal order, which is already embedded above.
This supplies a constructive CM−24 identification for the actual
source curve, independent of just repeating the Sun CM label.

The order remains faithfully embedded after every good reduction:
the polarized norm of[a]+[b]alpha_t is[a²+6b²], which is a
nonzero elliptic morphism for every nonzero pair of integers(a,b),
even when p divides that integer. However the FULL special-fibre
endomorphism ring may be larger. No assertion that it remains a
commutative maximal order is made.

Define the integral cohomology basis

    e_CM,t=(omega_t,psi_t),
    psi_t=eta_t+(t−1)omega_t,
    S_t=[[1,t−1],[0,1]], e_CM,t=e_Weier,t S_t.        (12)

Its determinant is1. Equation(8) implies
`alpha_t^*psi_t=−w psi_t+dG_t`, so its CLASS matrix is

    D_t=diag(w,−w).                                  (13)

The existing geometric GM coefficients at t²=1/2 also give
`psi_t=3 nabla_t omega_t−t omega_t`. This verifies the scalar
basis binding without pretending t is an elliptic endpoint or an
ambient first-jet calculation. A period-column convention would
transpose class-pullback matrices; no period value is chosen here.

## Genuine sigma-Frobenius and its precise constraints

Now fix an original p≡13,19mod24 and take O=W(Fp²), with its
coefficient Frobenius sigma. Choose the exact root t²=1/2 in O;
choose nu²=−3 in Z_p. Since (2/p)=−1 and(−3/p)=1,

    sigma(t)=−t, sigma(nu)=nu, sigma(w)=−w.          (14)

These are étale/Witt coefficient actions. Raw t^p generally differs
from−t modulo p²; no ambient coordinate-power map is substituted
for sigma in the following statement.

Let F: sigma^*H¹_cris(E_t/O)->H¹_cris(E_t/O) be genuine
one-step crystalline Frobenius, represented in the fixed integral
CM bases by

    F(sigma(e_CM,t))=e_CM,t M_CM.

Under good-lift comparison the basis(12) is a basis of this proper
integral cohomology. Frobenius functoriality for alpha_t gives

    D_t M_CM=M_CM sigma(D_t),
    sigma(D_t)=diag(−w,w).                           (15)

It is the conjugated endomorphism on the sigma source that occurs
on the right, not a commutation relation with the same scalar
matrix. Since 2w is a unit, the diagonal entries of M_CM are zero:

    M_CM=[[0,B],[C,0]], B,C in O.                    (16)

To justify its determinant, fix the algebraic cup convention
`<omega,eta>=Res_O((integral omega)eta)=1`. At infinity the local
coordinate q=−x/y gives omega=(1+O(q⁴))dq and
eta=(q^(−2)+O(q²))dq; only the leading primitive q contributes to
that residue. An opposite global sign convention would still be
a constant unit, and gives the same determinant relation. The
determinant-one change(12) preserves this pairing. Its scalar is
constant under sigma, rather than an unspecified parameter unit.
One-step crystalline Frobenius on H² is p times coefficient sigma.
Cup compatibility therefore reads

    M_CM^T [[0,1],[−1,0]] M_CM
       =p [[0,1],[−1,0]],
    det M_CM=p, BC=−p.                              (17)

Thus the determinant was not presumed merely from a shape ansatz.
The standard mod-p comparison with de Rham pullback also makes
F vanish on sigma of the Hodge line generated by omega: relative
Frobenius pulls back holomorphic differentials to zero. In(16)
that is the FIRST column, so

    C in pO, v_p(C)=1, B in O^*.                    (18)

The last two claims follow from(17) and integrality. In particular
the letter that is a unit is B, not C. These are constraints on
the actual, uniquely defined Frobenius. They do not evaluate B or
allow fitting it from an unknown target value. The argument uses
smooth good reduction and Hodge divisibility; it does not assume
ordinary reduction at this halfpoint.

In Weierstrass bases the sigma source changes by sigma(S_t), so
the corresponding class-pullback matrix must be

    M_Weier=S_t M_CM sigma(S_t)^(-1)
      =[[ (t−1)C, B+(t²−1)C ],
         [ C,       (t+1)C ]], t²−1=−1/2.            (19)

This checks Root's variance and entries. Replacing sigma(S_t) by
S_t, or using raw t^p as sigma(t), would give a different problem.
As usual composition with a functional transposes the cohomology
matrix, while the inverse-dual Frobenius structure uses the inverse
transpose over the isocrystal. No such change has been silently
made in(15)–(19).

## Delivered information and uncomputed input

The fixed map, complete kernel and exact terms(3)–(9), the
characteristic-zero CM embedding(11), and the integral CM basis
yield genuine semilinear constraints(16)–(19). The single unit B
